episodes.182259: Training showers and thunderstorms developed over central Pennsylvania during the evening of August 17, 2023, ahead of an approaching cold front. This convective activity  produced minor flooding across portions of southern Lycoming County and Sullivan County from the late evening of August 17 into the early morning hours of August 18. Rainfall of 2.24 was observed by a mobile weather station set up at the Little League World Series complex in South Williamsport.
episodes.182662: As the ridge of high pressure moved into a more favorable position near the Southern Plains, western Colorado was able to access the deeper monsoon moisture. This led to increased coverage of showers and thunderstorms. Storms were slow moving and produced heavy rain which led to some flooding in portions of Mesa County.
episodes.182712: An isolated severe thunderstorm produced localized wind damage over southern Maryland.
episodes.182720: Several thunderstorms developed ahead of a cold front, resulting in gale- to storm-force winds over area waterways.
episodes.182805: Two episodes of severe weather were observed over this period. The first, on August 18, was related to a ridge breakdown by a strong shortwave. Dry low and mid levels resulted in deep inverted-V profiles, which were conducive to strong wind gusts. ||The second episode of severe caliber gusts occurred on August 22nd. Moist southwesterly flow aloft, along with embedded shortwaves resulted in the developments of showers and thunderstorms across Central and Southwest Montana August 22nd. The area just experienced the remnants of Hurricane Hilary, which resulted in relatively moist lower levels, which in turn helped produce ample instability for severe thunderstorms.
episodes.183158: Strong storms moving southeastward produced strong wind gusts along the Brevard County coast.
episodes.183298: A high amplitude, negatively tilted trough moving across the Great Lakes and into New England along with cold and warm front provided strong forcing which resulted in flooding, wind damage, and 5 tornadoes. In the warm sector dewpoints surged into the mid 70s with PWATs near 2 inches which led to torrential downpours. Tornadoes occurred in Scotland, Ct, Scituate, RI, North Attleboro, MA, Stoughton, MA, and Weymouth, MA. The tornadoes ranged in intensity from EF-0 to EF-2.

episodes.184099: A cold front plowed across the lower Great Lakes region during the evening hours pushing a broken line of thunderstorms across western New York. Numerous marine thunderstorm wind reports were received as the line of thunderstorms moved through with even an isolated wind damage report over Niagara County. The cold air behind this front then helped spawn a waterspout late the following afternoon over southeast Lake Ontario.

episodes.184120: An upper-level low pressure system located west of the California coast and the subtropical high pressure located over New Mexico led to a south-southeast steering flow across Arizona. Thunderstorms developed during the afternoon hours across the higher terrain areas of southeastern Arizona and were steered north-northwestward into the south-central Arizona lower deserts with additional development occurring from outflow boundaries. Moderate instability was in place with MLCAPE values ranging between 500-1000 J/KG.
episodes.184463: An isolated severe wind gust occurred at the Livingston Airport.
episodes.184465: Several thunderstorms developed across the central and western portions of the Billings Forecast Area. These thunderstorms produced severe wind gusts due to large temperature/dew point spreads.
episodes.184605: An isolated supercell developed across western Nebraska and briefly brought damaging wind gust. The supercell was short lived and only an isolated damaging wind gust was observed.
episodes.184711: Slow-moving low pressure over Northeast Pennsylvania was the focus for a constant stream of heavy rain-producing thunderstorms during the overnight hours. A quick rainfall of 2.5 to 3.5 inches caused swollen streams and areas of flooding. Water washed out several roads and infiltrated a mobile home park near Hallstead, PA forcing several people from their homes in the middle of the night.
episodes.184714: An upper level trough as a cold front approached at the surface. Just before a line of thunderstorms reached our area along the cold front, thunderstorms developed over our area in a zone of low-level warm advection. This moisture eventually interacted with the storms along the cold front and helped strengthen them. Severe thunderstorms developed and produced damaging winds in southern CT.
episodes.184715: An upper level trough as a cold front approached at the surface. Just before a line of thunderstorms reached our area along the cold front, thunderstorms developed over our area in a zone of low-level warm advection. This moisture eventually interacted with the storms along the cold front and helped strengthen them. Severe thunderstorms developed and produced damaging winds over the waters.
episodes.184803: A 59 mph wind gust measured near Camas.
episodes.184838: A waterspout formed late in the day across eastern Lake Ontario offshore of Pulaski.
episodes.184937: A fresh push of monsoon moisture fueled another round of thunderstorms over northwest Arizona. Several storms produced flash flooding and damaging winds.
episodes.184938: A fresh push of monsoon moisture fueled scattered thunderstorms over southern Nevada. Isolated flash flooding and damaging winds occurred.
episodes.185027: Monsoonal flash flooding brought a variety of impacts to southern Utah, including flash flooding in Capitol Reef National Park that prompted evacuation of a campground and road closures.
episodes.185258: Isolated severe thunderstorm along a frontal boundary produced damaging winds across portions of southeast Virginia.

episodes.186599: A cold front swept eastward from southeastern Lower MI and northeastern IN to central Lake Erie and northeast OH during the evening of the 17th. Ahead of the front, several lines of multicell showers and thunderstorms persisted generally eastward across northeast OH and produced isolated damaging convective wind gusts in Trumbull County. These storms encountered weak to moderate MUCAPE and moderate to strong effective bulk shear.
episodes.186600: A cold front swept eastward from southeastern Lower MI and northeastern IN to central Lake Erie and northeast OH during the evening of the 17th. Ahead of the front, several lines of multicell showers and thunderstorms persisted generally eastward across northeast OH. One storm generated a gale-force peak convective wind gust along the Lake County shore. These storms encountered weak to moderate MUCAPE and moderate to strong effective bulk shear.

A tornado caused damage in the town of Scotland, located in|Windham County, CT. The tornado touched down on Bass Road and continued along Route 14 (Huntington Road) and crossed Pinch Street before it eventually|lifted near Brook Road. While there wasn't much in the way of structural damage observed, other than gutter damage to two homes, there was significant tree|damage. It was estimated that well over one hundred trees were|either downed or sheared off at their tops.
In Scotland, there were trees and large branches down.

A tornado caused significant damage along a discontinuous path|in Scituate, Johnston, and North Providence, Rhode Island. This |is the strongest tornado to have struck Rhode Island since the F-2|tornado in Cranston and Providence on August 7, 1986.||The tornado first touched down near Byron Randall Road in Scituate|which is where the most severe damage occurred. There were hundreds|of large trees either uprooted or snapped at their bases. One |home sustained damage to its roof, the top of its chimney was |blown off, windows were blown in, and an exterior door was |dislodged from its framing. Damage was consistent with winds of |around 115 mph which is classified as EF-2 on the Enhanced Fujita|Scale.||The tornado then tracked into Johnston where it crossed I-295 at |Exit 10 and lifted a vehicle into the air before dropping it back |onto the highway. The driver was transported to an area hospital |with minor injuries. From there, the tornado moved across Bridle |Way and Carriage Way where a number of trees were snapped or |uprooted, some of which fell onto homes or vehicles. Some homes |also lost some singles from their roofs. A metal Stop sign pole |was bent in half and the sign was blown away. The tornado then |caused damage in Highland Memorial Park Cemetery where a number of|large trees were either snapped or uprooted. The damage observed |in Johnston was consistent with winds of 90 to 100 mph which is |classified as EF-1 on the Enhanced Fujita Scale.||Finally, the tornado crossed into North Providence. Similar to|Johnston, a number of trees were either snapped or uprooted, some|falling onto homes or vehicles. Most of the damage observed was to|the north of Mineral Spring Avenue. One of the harder hit areas  |included Lydia Avenue, Armand Drive, and Bennett Street where two|homes were made uninhabitable from fallen trees. The damage |observed in North Providence was consistent with winds of 90 to |100 mph which is classified as EF-1 on the Enhanced Fujita Scale.||The National Weather Service would like to thank the Rhode Island|Emergency Management Agency, the Scituate Police Department, the|Johnston Police Department, the North Providence Fire Department,|and Skywarn Amateur Radio Operators for their assistance with the|damage survey.
